IS: 8231 -1976 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
CLIPS, PAPER, SPRING TYPE 



( Reaffirmed 2004 )

1. Scope — The materials, dimensions and performance requirements for spring type paper clips 
used to hold papers. 

2. Types — The paper clips shall be of Type 1 and Type 2. 

2.1 The Type 1 clips shall consist of two hinged wire handles and a spring. 

2.2 The Type 2 clips shall consist of two die-stamped handles and a cylindrical spring or coil 
spring. 

3. Materials 

3.1 Spring — Cold rolled spring steel of suitable hardness to satisfy the requirements mentioned in 
the subsequent classes. 

3.2 Handles for Type 1 Clips— Hard drawn steel wire suitable for particular size of clip. They shall 
retain their original rigidity and shape during normal use. 

4. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1, 2 and 3 and Table 1 and Table 2.

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 The handles when pressed together shall cause the jaws of the clips to open. 

5.2 A hole shall be provided in the handles of the clips for hanging them. 

5.3 Two slits of equal width shall be provided on the cylindrical spring for inserting the handles. 

5.4 The width of the cylindrical spring and the gripping edge of the handle shall be equal up 
to 63 mm wide. 

5.5 The spring shall not be detachable from the jaws or the jaws shall become misaligned during 
normal use in Type 2 clips, 

5.6 The gripping shall be uniform throughout the jaws. 

5.7 The clips shall be free from burrs, sharp edges which may affect the appearance or service- 
ability or hazardous to the user. 

5.8 The surfaces shall be protected by a suitable finish. The finish shall not crack, chip or scale 
and shall leave no mark on paper. The surfaces may be nickel or chromium coated conforming to 
IS: 1068-1968 'Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on iron and steel 
( first revision ) '. 

5.9 The clips may be blue finished, if required by the consumer. 

2 



IS: 8231 -1976 
6. Tests 

fi.1 Holding Strength — Insert paper sheet 0'12 mm thick between the jaws of the clips. Suspend 
the weight from the paper as given in Table 3. The clips shall hold the specified weight without the 
paper slipping at any point in the jaws.

6.3 Capacity - Insert a block of wood of thickness as specified in Table 5 between the jaws of 
clips. Remove the block after 24 hours and insert a sheet of 32 M bond paper. The clips shall 
hold the paper family. The spring shall not fracture at any point after the block of wood is 
removed.

6-4 Corrosion Resistance — Dip the clips in a solution of mineral spirit to remove the surface film or 
grease ^nd wipe dry. Place the clips in a boiling 10 percent aqueous solution of sodium chloride 
for 15 minutes. Remove it from the solution and immediately place them in a similar solution at 
room temperature for 24 hours. Allow it to dry at room temperature without wiping. Rinse the 
clips in luke warm water. Allow them to dry and examine the clips for signs of corrosion. There 
shall not be any sign of corrosion. 

7. Marking 

7.1 The clips shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark and 
size. 

7.2 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing— -The clips may be packed as agreed to betweenihe purchaser and the supplier.
